review_candidates.title: Principal Data Systems Software Engineer
review_candidates.description: Job Description Build the next generation of Oracle Zero Data Loss Recovery Appliance (ZDLRA) software, helping fortune 500 enterprises protect and recover their business-critical Oracle databases. Work on software where data integrity, recoverability, cyber resilience, and performance at scale directly affect customers' most important operations. Join our growing engineering team in Bengaluru and collaborate with experienced ZDLRA engineers in India and the US. You will contribute to shared product priorities, deliver new features and projects, and help evolve an enterprise data protection platform. This role offers the opportunity to help shape a new team while building deep product expertise within an established global engineering organization. The work spans Oracle database kernel development and systems programming, primarily in C and PL/SQL on Linux. You will tackle engineering problems involving buffers and caches, memory management, storage, file systems, I/O, networking, concurrency, and distributed systems. Strong algorithms, thoughtful design, and an understanding of how these components interact will be central to delivering correct, efficient, and maintainable software. You will participate throughout the development lifecycle: understanding problems, exploring the codebase, identifying root causes, designing solutions, implementing changes, writing tests, and validating results. The work combines new development and enhancements with complex defect resolution, including issues encountered in customer environments. As your product knowledge grows, you will take increasing technical ownership of assigned features and components, contributing to design decisions, code reviews, ongoing maintenance, and knowledge sharing. We value engineers who investigate problems systematically, use documentation and diagnostic tools resourcefully, communicate clearly, and help colleagues succeed. You will use modern engineering tools, including LLMs and AI coding agents, to accelerate code exploration, development, and testing while applying independent judgment and rigorous validation to the resulting designs and code. We welcome experienced developers with strong C, Linux, system programming skills and practical knowledge of database internals, storage, distributed systems, or other demanding enterprise software. Prior Oracle Database, RMAN, PL/SQL, or backup and recovery product experience is an advantage. Strong systems fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to translate complex requirements into reliable production software are essential. This position is based in Bengaluru, India. Responsibilities Product development and technical ownership Design, implement, and maintain ZDLRA features and enhancements in C and PL/SQL on Linux, contributing to Oracle database kernel and systems software development. Translate requirements and technical problems into clear designs, manageable tasks, and deliverable milestones. Evaluate alternatives and document trade-offs involving correctness, performance, scalability, compatibility, and maintainability. Apply appropriate algorithms and data structures to build efficient, reliable software. Reason about memory use, concurrency, synchronization, and behavior under demanding workloads. Develop and improve assigned components involving buffers, caches, storage, file systems, I/O, networking, and distributed processing, with careful attention to data integrity and recovery behavior. Build product expertise through code exploration, technical documentation, collaboration, and delivery of fixes and enhancements. Progress toward ownership of assigned features and projects, including subsequent development, maintenance, and defect resolution. Investigation, performance, and quality Investigate complex defects, including issues reported from customer deployments. Reproduce failures, trace relevant code paths, establish root causes, and implement durable fixes. Use GDB, core dumps, logs, traces, profiling tools, and Linux utilities to gather evidence and understand software behavior across interacting components. Diagnose performance and scalability bottlenecks involving CPU, memory, storage, I/O, and networking. Establish useful measurements and validate the impact of changes against representative workloads. Design and implement tests alongside production code. Cover functional behavior, boundary conditions, regressions, concurrency, and relevant failure and recovery scenarios using the team's engineering and test frameworks. Use shell scripting and automation to improve diagnostic data collection, issue reproduction, testing, and other repeatable development tasks. Follow secure coding practices and engineering standards. Evaluate error handling, resource management, backward compatibility, and versioning implications when modifying existing code or interfaces. Engineering execution and collaboration Take assigned work through the software development lifecycle, from analysis and design through implementation, review, testing, integration, and maintenance. Plan work realistically, identify dependencies, and communicate progress, design decisions, risks, and blockers. Coordinate with the engineering team to deliver agreed project milestones. Collaborate closely with ZDLRA engineers in India and the US and with relevant database engineering teams to resolve cross-component issues and deliver shared product objectives. Participate in design and code reviews, providing constructive feedback on correctness, clarity, performance, security, test coverage, and long-term maintainability. Write and maintain useful design notes, implementation documentation, and troubleshooting guidance. Share findings so that investigations and engineering decisions benefit the wider team. Use internal documentation, specifications, and existing code resourcefully to understand unfamiliar areas. Ask focused questions, seek timely feedback, and help colleagues solve technical problems. As product expertise grows, provide technical guidance, mentor colleagues, and contribute to improvements in the team's development practices and engineering quality. AI-assisted engineering Use LLMs and AI coding agents to accelerate code exploration, problem analysis, implementation, test development, and documentation where they are useful. Critically review AI-generated suggestions and verify them against the actual codebase, requirements, and observed behavior. Validate changes through appropriate reviews and tests, and remain accountable for the correctness, security, performance, and maintainability of delivered software. Break down system-level specifications into clear, testable software requirements. Maintain requirement documents and ensure traceability from requirements to design and testing. Software Integration & Release: Integrate software components, drivers, and application code from various teams into a cohesive and functional software build. Develop and maintain the software build environment, including build automation scripts (CMake, Python) and Continuous Integration (CI/CD) pipelines (Jenkins, GitLab). Manage source code repositories (Git), including branching, merging, and release tagging strategies. Flash integrated software onto target hardware (OBC, DCDC, etc.), perform initial hardware bring-up, and conduct smoke tests to verify core functionality. Architecture & Design Support: Assist in the creation and documentation of software architecture and detailed design artifacts. Participate in design and code reviews to ensure requirements are met and architectural principles are followed. Support the link between high-level requirements and low-level implementation, ensuring a clear and logical flow. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Act as a key technical bridge between systems engineering, hardware design, software development, and validation teams. Investigate, analyze, and resolve complex software integration issues, build failures, and on-target problems. Contribute to process improvements across the software development lifecycle, championing best practices in line with standards like A-SPICE. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. 1+ years of experience in an embedded software development, integration, or systems engineering role. Solid programming skills in C. Strong understanding of the full software development lifecycle (e.g., V-Model, Agile/Scrum). Experience with version control systems, particularly Git. Proficiency in at least one scripting language (e.g., Python). Hands-on experience with build systems (e.g., Make/CMake) and compilers/linkers for embedded systems. Experience with software architecture and design modeling. Knowledge of AUTOSAR architecture, including experience with RTE (Runtime Environment) configuration. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a hands-on, detail-oriented mindset. Strong communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience in the automotive industry, especially with power electronics like On-Board Chargers (OBC), DC-DC converters, or Inverters. Experience with requirements management tools (e.g.,Polarion) Hands-on experience with Continuous Integration (CI) framework and tools (e.g., Jenkins). Knowledge of software diagnostics (e.g., UDS, DTCs) and communication protocols (e.g., CAN, LIN). Familiarity with automotive software standards like AUTOSAR and functional safety (ISO 26262). Familiarity with process models like Automotive SPICE (A-SPICE). Experience with embedded microcontrollers (e.g., Infineon Aurix) and hardware debuggers (e.g., Lauterbach TRACE32, UDE). Understanding of model-based development (MBD) using tools like MATLAB/Simulink is a plus.

review_candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer (Full Stack)
review_candidates.description: Who We Are 4C Strategies builds readiness and resilience software for defence, public safety and critical infrastructure organisations in more than 70 countries. Our Exonaut® platform is used to plan, run and evaluate large-scale training, exercises and capability evaluations, and our consultants and engineers work alongside those organisations across Europe, North America and beyond. What We're Building We're building the evidence layer for defence experimentation and evaluation. When an organisation tests a new capability — a sensor, an autonomous system, a different way of operating — it has to be able to defend the result afterwards, to someone who was not there and who has every reason to challenge it. Today that evidence lives in spreadsheets, documents and standalone survey tools, and it cannot be traced from a conclusion back to the observation that supports it. Our platform fixes the structure before the data is collected, captures evidence from people and from machines, fuses it into chains that carry their own provenance, and keeps every finding traceable to its source. The hard part is not the plumbing. It is holding one coherent model steady while every customer arrives with their own vocabulary, their own method and a reasonable-sounding request for one more special case. How We Build Modern Java — currently 25 — and Spring Boot on a modular JPMS architecture, an Angular 21 single-page application, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, deployed to Kubernetes. The principles are conservative on purpose. Dependency inversion at every module boundary: contracts in an API module, implementation separate, no reverse dependencies. Schema evolution is explicit and reversible, through migrations with rollback scripts and no auto-DDL in any environment. Evolutionary change over rewrites, with a staged path when a domain concern outgrows its boundary. Structural decisions are argued in RFCs and recorded in ADRs, and changes to the core domain model go through that process rather than around it — because that model is the product, and it is the thing most easily damaged under delivery pressure. Three constraints shape most of what we do. It runs inside the customer's own environment: single-tenant, sovereign, accredited, sometimes with no route to the internet at all, so nothing may assume a managed cloud service. Evidence has to be captured where the work happens, which means a tablet in a field with no connectivity and a sync that loses nothing. And the audit trail is immutable — evidence cannot be quietly deleted or backdated, and no automated process publishes a conclusion without a person taking responsibility for it. You We are a small team, so you will work across the stack rather than behind a specialism. Substantial experience in either Java or TypeScript, and a genuine willingness to be useful in the other. Sound judgement about data modelling, because most of the interesting problems here are modelling problems wearing engineering clothes. Comfortable with ambiguity: requirements move, and the shape of the answer is often the work. A real advantage, though none of it is required: sovereign, air-gapped or accredited deployments; offline-first or sync-heavy applications; geospatial data; sensor, telemetry or simulation integration; audit and traceability requirements. The domain is learnable, the judgement less so. The team is small enough that your work is visible and your arguments carry. Your designs will be challenged and you will be expected to challenge back — including on scope. Research shows some people only apply when they meet every requirement. If you don't tick every box but recognise yourself in much of the above, please apply anyway. We'd genuinely like to hear from you. Security and citizenship This role supports defence work, so the successful candidate must hold Swedish citizenship and pass Swedish security vetting (säkerhetsprövning). We will explain what the check involves early in the process rather than late — a requirement like this should never be a surprise at offer stage. This requirement comes only from the security rules that govern defence work, not from personal preference. Why it matters Capability decisions get made on this evidence. When an organisation concludes that something is ready, or that it is not, that judgement has consequences for the people who depend on it. Making it defensible is the whole point. How We Hire Every interview has a written script and a scored rubric, applied the same way to every candidate. Hiring Manager Screen — a conversation about your experience, how you work and what you want next. System Design — a design discussion drawn from problems like the ones above. Programming — a hands-on session in a language of your choice (Java, C#, TypeScript, Python or Go). Culture Interview — how you collaborate, disagree and make decisions with others. Candidate Q&A — your time to interrogate us. We expect you to use it. We then debrief as a panel and decide. We review applications on a rolling basis. What You Can Expect From 4C Strategies Stockholm-based, with hybrid working. Competitive salary, reviewed annually. Occupational pension (tjänstepension). Wellness allowance (friskvårdsbidrag). Healthcare insurance, including insurance for treatment. Parental pay. Vaccinations. A supportive, collaborative team building meaningful products for mission-critical work. Why join 4C Strategies This is a small team with a large surface. You will not be handed a narrow lane: the platform is still being shaped, the domain model is still being argued about, and the person who makes the argument well is the person who decides. If you would rather own a hard, open problem end to end than take tickets from a backlog, that is the job. The work matters: what you build helps defence, public safety and resilience organisations prepare for the situations they hope not to face. How To Apply To apply, click the Apply today button and submit your CV. A short cover note on your experience and motivation is welcome but not required. We review applications on a rolling basis, so please apply as soon as you can. 4C Strategies is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

We're building the most advanced crypto casino platform in the world—and we’re just getting started. You’ll play a key role in shaping our game architecture, improving performance and player experience, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver innovative, next-generation gaming experiences. This is a fully remote role. We value autonomy, trust, and flexibility—and expect you to bring energy, ownership, and leadership wherever you work. What You’ll Be Doing Lead the design, development, and optimization of web-based game experiences using PixiJS and React for high-performance rendering Architect and implement scalable back-end services using Node.js, integrating real-time gameplay features such as multiplayer, leaderboards, and in-game events Collaborate with product, design, and backend teams to translate game concepts into performant, interactive experiences Optimize client-server communication (e.g., WebSockets, REST APIs) to ensure seamless, low-latency gameplay Apply game development best practices to improve performance, scalability, and maintainability across multiple projects Build and maintain automated CI/CD pipelines to enable rapid, reliable deployment of game features and updates Contribute to technical strategy, code reviews, and mentoring of junior engineers Technologies You’ll Work With Core Infrastructure React PixiJS NodeJS Typescript PostgreSQL Redis RabbitMQ Bonus Skills (Nice To Have Experience With) Datadog AWS CI/CD Pipelines Must-Haves What We’re Looking For: 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a focus on game or interactive application development Strong expertise in PixiJS (or other HTML5/WebGL frameworks) and/or React for high-performance front-end experiences Proficiency with Node.js and building scalable back-end services, architecture Experience with CI/CD pipelines and modern development workflows Nice-to-Have Background in crypto or iGaming Background in multiplayer gaming, gambling, or iGaming platforms Familiarity with game networking protocols, animations, and physics engines Experience leading technical initiatives or mentoring engineers Knowledge of cloud deployment (AWS) and containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes, ECS) Why Join over99.com ? Be part of a fast-growing and well-funded start-up at the intersection of gaming and blockchain Work with a world-class engineering team—collaborative, autonomous, and impact-driven Build next-generation systems with full ownership over architecture and implementation Remote-first culture with flexible hours, asynchronous communication, and no micromanagement A product and mission you’ll actually be excited about What You’ll Get Why join us? 💸 Competitive Salary - We pay top-of-market for top-tier talent 🌐 Remote-First Work Environment - Work from anywhere, collaborate globally 🏖️ Generous Holiday Allowance - Take the time you need to rest and recharge 🕒 Flexible Time Off & Hours - We focus on output, not clocking in 🎯 Performance-Related Bonus - We reward real impact. Hit goals, share the upside Ready to Build with Us? We’re creating something bold and different—and we want the best minds to help us do it. If you're passionate about infrastructure, performance, and pushing tech boundaries, apply now and let’s build the future of crypto gaming together.
